xenophon.s: Xenophon was an Athenian soldier, historian and philosopher of the late fifth and fourth centuries BCE, a pupil of Socrates. He served with the Greek mercenaries hired by Cyrus the Younger in 401 BCE and led their retreat after Cyrus's death.

xerxes-i.s: Xerxes I was king of the Achaemenid Empire from 486 to 465 BCE, the son and successor of Darius I. He led the great invasion of Greece in 480 BCE, which won at Thermopylae and sacked Athens but was defeated at Salamis and, in 479 BCE, at Plataea.

xianbei.s: The Xianbei were a nomadic people of the eastern Eurasian steppe, in present-day Mongolia and Manchuria. After the decline of the Xiongnu, they became the dominant power on the northern steppe in the second century CE.

xiang-army.s: The Xiang Army was a regional military force raised in Hunan province by the scholar-official Zeng Guofan to fight the Taiping Rebellion. Its success, together with Li Hongzhang's Huai Army, was crucial in suppressing the Taiping.

xiang-jun.s: The xiang jun was the professional standing army of the Song Dynasty. It was very large, with estimates of over one million men under arms at its peak.

xiang-yu.s: Xiang Yu was a Chinese military leader who led the rebellion against the Qin dynasty and became the dominant warlord after its fall. He then fought Liu Bang for control of China in the Chu–Han contention.

xiangyang.s: Xiangyang is a city on the Han River in central China, which with its twin city Fancheng formed the gateway to the Yangtze valley. The Mongol siege of Xiangyang from 1267 to 1273 was the pivotal confrontation in the conquest of the Southern Song.

xing-ware.s: Xing ware is a type of white porcelain produced at kilns in northern China under the Tang Dynasty. Its fine white body made it one of the earliest high-quality porcelains.

xinhai-revolution.s: The Xinhai Revolution was the revolution of 1911 that overthrew the Qing Empire and ended imperial rule in China. It was triggered by a military mutiny at Wuchang and spread rapidly as provinces declared independence.

xinjiang.s: Xinjiang is a large region in north-western China, including the Tarim Basin and Dzungaria, historically home to oasis cities on the Silk Road. Its eastern parts formed part of the domains of the Chagatai Empire and its successors.

xiongnu-civil-war.s: The Xiongnu civil war was a succession conflict among rival claimants to the position of chanyu that split the Xiongnu Empire around 57 BCE. The confederation divided between factions led by Huhanye, who submitted to the Han Dynasty, and his brother Zhizhi, who moved westward.

xiongnu-empire.s: The Xiongnu Empire was a confederation of nomadic peoples that dominated the eastern Eurasian steppe from the late third century BCE to the first century CE. Under the chanyu Modu it united the steppe tribes and became a formidable rival of the Han Dynasty, extracting tribute…

xoconusco.s: Xoconusco, or Soconusco, is a region on the Pacific coast of southern Mexico, in modern Chiapas, renowned for its cacao. The ruler Ahuitzotl extended the empire south to Xoconusco and into what is now Guatemala.

xuanwu-gate-incident.s: The Xuanwu Gate Incident was a palace coup in 626 CE in which Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers, the crown prince Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, at the Xuanwu Gate of the Tang palace in Chang'an. His father, Emperor Gaozu, soon abdicated in his favour.

xwastak.s: Xwastak was the land tax of the Sasanian Empire. The fiscal system rested on this tax, assessed on agricultural production.

xiao-baojuan.s: Xiao Baojuan was emperor of the Southern Qi dynasty from 498 to 501, posthumously demoted to Marquess of Donghun. His reign was remembered for extravagance and the killing of ministers, generals and relatives.

xue-ju.s: Xue Ju was a wealthy local leader of Jincheng, modern Lanzhou, who rebelled in 617 as the Sui dynasty collapsed and proclaimed himself emperor of Qin. His armies controlled much of Gansu and defeated the young Tang prince Li Shimin in 618, but Xue Ju died soon afterwards.

xue-rengao.s: Xue Rengao was the second and last ruler of the short-lived Qin state founded by his father Xue Ju in the north-west during the collapse of the Sui dynasty. He succeeded in 618 after Qin had beaten Tang forces at Qianshuiyuan, but later that year Li Shimin, the future Emperor…

xanana-gusmao.s: Xanana Gusmão is an East Timorese independence leader who commanded the Fretilin resistance against Indonesian occupation from 1981 until his capture in 1992. After the 1999 independence referendum he became the first President of East Timor in 2002 and later served as prime…

xavier-coppolani.s: Xavier Coppolani was a Corsican-born French colonial administrator and scholar of Islamic brotherhoods. From 1902 he pursued a policy of peaceful penetration in Mauritania, using alliances with religious leaders to bring the emirates of Trarza and Brakna under French…

xi-gui.s: Xi Gui was the wife of the Marquis of Xi, a small Zhou state, whose story is told in the Zuo zhuan. An insult to her by the Marquis of Cai drew Chu into the region; King Wen of Chu destroyed Xi around 680 BCE and took her as his wife, and by tradition she bore him the future…

xia-yue.s: Xia Yue was the deputy through whom Chen Yu, chief minister of Zhao, governed the Kingdom of Dai after the fall of the Qin. In 205 BCE the Han general Han Xin defeated and captured him, opening the way for the destruction of the Zhao army at Jingxing the following year.

xiao-cong.s: Xiao Cong was the third and last emperor of the Western Liang, a client state at Jiangling on the middle Yangtze. In 587 Emperor Wen of Sui summoned him to Chang'an and abolished the state; Xiao Cong was given a noble title, and his sister was the empress of Emperor Yang of Sui.

xiao-daocheng.s: Xiao Daocheng was a general who became the power behind the Liu Song throne in southern China. In 479 he forced Emperor Shun to abdicate and founded the Southern Qi dynasty, reigning as Emperor Gao until 482 and attempting to restore order to state finances.

xiao-defei.s: Xiao Defei was the wife of Yelü Chun, the Liao prince proclaimed emperor at Yanjing in 1122, founding the Northern Liao. After his death within months she governed as empress dowager, but when the Jurchen ruler Aguda took Yanjing at the end of 1122 she fled and was later…

xiao-he.s: Xiao He was the chancellor of Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty. He secured the Qin archives when the rebels took Xianyang, kept the armies supplied from Guanzhong and Sichuan during the war with Xiang Yu, and as first chancellor of the Han drafted its laws on Qin models.

xicotencatl-the-elder.s: Xicotencatl the Elder was one of the four rulers of Tlaxcala in central Mexico. After Tlaxcala fought Hernán Cortés in 1519, he and Maxixcatzin led its alliance with the Spaniards, supplying thousands of warriors for the conquest of Tenochtitlan, while his son Xicotencatl the…

xu-shouhui.s: Xu Shouhui was a leader of the southern Red Turban rebellion against the Yuan dynasty. In 1351 he proclaimed the Tianwan regime on the middle Yangtze, but power passed to his officer Chen Youliang, who murdered him in 1360 and founded the Chen Han state, prompting commanders…

xu-wen.s: Xu Wen was a general of the Wu kingdom of the Ten Kingdoms period. After Yang Xingmi's death he seized control of the government from the weak Yang heirs and ruled as regent, while his adopted son Xu Zhigao ran affairs from Jinling; in 937 Xu Zhigao took the throne and founded…

xuanzang.s: Xuanzang was a Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar and traveller who journeyed overland to India between 629 and 645 to collect scriptures. He studied at Nalanda, visited the court of Harsha, and on his return translated many texts into Chinese.

xu-shuzheng.s: Xu Shuzheng was a Chinese general and politician of the Anhui clique during the Beiyang period. In 1919 he led troops into Urga and forced the abolition of Outer Mongolia's autonomy, but his rule there collapsed when the Anhui clique lost power in 1920.

xochitecatl.s: Xochitécatl is an archaeological site in southern Tlaxcala, Mexico, on a hill beside Cacaxtla. First occupied in the Formative period, it has a circular Pyramid of the Spiral and other pyramids, and was reused as a ceremonial centre in the Epiclassic period, when Cacaxtla…

xavante.s: The Xavante are a Gê-speaking indigenous people of central Brazil. In the 18th century they lived in Goiás, where they clashed with settlers and some were gathered into government villages, before moving west into Mato Grosso.

xin-dynasty.s: The Xin dynasty was the short-lived regime of Wang Mang, who usurped the throne of the Han dynasty in 9 CE and proclaimed a "new" (xin) dynasty. His reforms, including the nationalisation of land, a ban on the sale of slaves and repeated changes of currency, caused disorder,…

xenophanes.s: Xenophanes of Colophon was a Greek poet and philosopher who left Ionia after the Persian conquest and spent a long life wandering the Greek world, especially Sicily. In surviving fragments of his verse he mocked the human-like gods of Homer and Hesiod and argued for a single,…

xingyang.s: Xingyang is a county-level city in Henan province, China, west of Zhengzhou near the southern bank of the Yellow River. Its position at the eastern end of the hill country guarding the approaches to Luoyang made it strategically important in early Chinese history, most…

xie-an.s: Xie An was a Chinese statesman of the Eastern Jin dynasty and head of the aristocratic Xie clan. Long a celebrated recluse, he entered office in his forties, became chief minister and checked the ambitions of the general Huan Wen.

xie-xuan.s: Xie Xuan was a Chinese general of the Eastern Jin dynasty and nephew of the statesman Xie An. In 377 he raised the Beifu, or 'Northern Headquarters', army at Jingkou from refugees from the north, which became the dynasty's best fighting force.

xois.s: Xois was an ancient city in the northern Nile Delta of Egypt, near the modern town of Sakha in Kafr el-Sheikh Governorate. In Manetho's history of Egypt it is the seat of the Fourteenth Dynasty, whose kings he calls Xoites, although modern scholars mostly place that dynasty at…

xichong-county.s: Xichong is a county in the north-east of Sichuan province in China, administered by the city of Nanchong. It is known in history as the area where Zhang Xianzhong, founder of the short-lived Great Xi regime in Sichuan, was killed in battle with Qing forces under Hooge in early…

xingtai.s: Xingtai is a city in southern Hebei, China, at the eastern foot of the Taihang Mountains, and one of the oldest cities of northern China, once the centre of the Zhou-era state of Xing. As Xiangguo it was the capital of Zhang Er's kingdom of Changshan in 206 BCE and, from 319…

xuzhou.s: Pengcheng was the ancient name of Xuzhou in northern Jiangsu, China. A key crossroads of the North China Plain, it was the capital of Xiang Yu's Western Chu after 206 BCE, and in 205 BCE Xiang Yu routed Liu Bang's much larger army there in the Battle of Pengcheng.

xiao-tong.s: Xiao Tong, known posthumously as Crown Prince Zhaoming, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty in southern China. A devout Buddhist and patron of letters, he gathered scholars at his court and directed the compilation of the Wen Xuan, the most influential…

xie-lingyun.s: Xie Lingyun was a Chinese poet of the Eastern Jin and Liu Song dynasties, a member of the aristocratic Xie clan who held the title Duke of Kangle. He is regarded as the founder of Chinese landscape poetry (shanshui), describing the mountains and rivers of the south from his…

xanthos.s: Xanthos was the chief city of ancient Lycia, on the Xanthos (Eşen) river in south-western Turkey. Herodotus says its citizens destroyed themselves rather than surrender to the Persian general Harpagus around 540 BCE, and the city later raised the pillar tombs of the Lycian…

xishuangbanna.s: Xishuangbanna, in Tai Sipsongpanna, 'twelve thousand rice fields', is a region in the far south of Yunnan, China, bordering Laos and Myanmar, now the Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture. It was the home of a Tai Lue kingdom centred on Chiang Hung (Jinghong), which paid…

xiangtangshan-caves.s: The Xiangtangshan Caves are Buddhist cave temples near Handan in Hebei province, China. They were carved in the mid-6th century under the Northern Qi dynasty, whose emperors kept a residence nearby, and contain large sculptures of the Buddha in a fuller, rounded style.

xuantu-commandery.s: Xuantu Commandery was a commandery set up by the Han dynasty of China in 107 BCE, after its conquest of Gojoseon, in the north of the Korean peninsula and southern Manchuria. Pressure from local peoples, above all the rising Goguryeo, forced it to move north-west towards…

xuanming-calendar.s: The Xuanming calendar was an astronomical calendar compiled in Tang China and adopted in 822. It reached Japan with an embassy from Balhae and was introduced there in 862 as the Senmyō calendar, which Japan then used, without official revision, for more than 800 years, until…

xhosa-people.s: The Xhosa are a Bantu-speaking people of the Eastern Cape in South Africa, speaking isiXhosa. In the late eighteenth and nineteenth centuries they fought a long series of frontier wars against the Cape Colony, lost much of their land and suffered the cattle-killing movement of…

xie-shi.s: Xie Shi was a general of the Eastern Jin dynasty and younger brother of the minister Xie An. In 383 he was the overall commander, with his nephew Xie Xuan, of the Jin forces that defeated the huge invading army of Fu Jian of the Former Qin at the Battle of Fei River.

xu-jing.s: Xu Jing was a Chinese official of the Song dynasty who travelled to Goryeo as a member of an embassy in 1123. He wrote an illustrated account of the kingdom, the Gaoli tujing, describing its capital, government, customs and crafts.

xiao-yanyan.s: Xiao Yanyan, known as Empress Dowager Chengtian, was the widow of Emperor Jingzong of Liao and regent for her son Shengzong from 982 until her death in 1009. A capable ruler and military commander, she reformed the government and in 1004 led the campaign against the Song that…

xar-moron-river.s: The Xar Moron is a river of eastern Inner Mongolia, China, and the main upper branch of the Liao River. Its basin, with that of the Laoha River, was the homeland of the Khitan, where they founded their capital Shangjing, and earlier of Neolithic cultures such as Hongshan.

xian-incident.s: The Xi'an Incident was the detention of Chiang Kai-shek in Xi'an in December 1936 by his own generals Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng, who wanted him to stop fighting the Communists and resist Japan. After about two weeks of negotiations, in which the Communists took part,…

xinca-people.s: The Xinca are an indigenous people of south-eastern Guatemala, living mainly in the department of Santa Rosa and neighbouring areas near the Pacific coast. Unlike most indigenous Guatemalans they are not Maya, and their language, Xinca, is unrelated to the Mayan languages.

xiomara-castro.s: Xiomara Castro (born 1959) is a Honduran politician who was president from January 2022 to January 2026, the first woman to hold the office. The wife of former president Manuel Zelaya, she led the resistance movement after his removal in 2009 and co-founded the left-wing Libre…

xibeigang.s: Xibeigang is the royal cemetery of the late Shang dynasty at Yinxu, on the north bank of the Huan River near Anyang in Henan. Excavated by Academia Sinica in the 1930s and later by Chinese archaeologists, it contains large cross-shaped shaft tombs, generally attributed to…

xia-shang-zhou-chronology-project.s: The Xia–Shang–Zhou Chronology Project was a research programme sponsored by the People's Republic of China from 1996 to 2000 to establish dates for China's first three dynasties. Combining texts, astronomy, radiocarbon dating and archaeology, it dated the start of the Xia to…

xitle.s: Xitle is a small volcanic cone on the slopes of the Ajusco massif in the south of Mexico City. Its eruption produced the lava field of the Pedregal and buried the early city of Cuicuilco, contributing to the decline of Teotihuacan's main rival in the Basin of Mexico.

xue-rengui.s: Xue Rengui was a Tang dynasty general who rose to fame in Emperor Taizong's campaign against Goguryeo in 645 and later served in the Tang conquest of Korea. In 670 he led a large Tang army against the Tibetan Empire but was routed at the Dafei River near Lake Kokonor by the…

xianyun.s: The Xianyun were a people of the north-western frontier of the Western Zhou, known from bronze inscriptions and the Book of Songs, who repeatedly raided the Zhou heartland in the Wei valley in the ninth and eighth centuries BCE. King Xuan's campaigns against them are recorded…

xu-da.s: Xu Da was a Chinese general and the leading commander of Zhu Yuanzhang, founder of the Ming dynasty. He fought in the wars against Chen Youliang and Zhang Shicheng and in 1368 led the northern expedition that took the Yuan capital Dadu, renamed Beiping.

xuanzheng-yuan.s: The Xuanzheng Yuan, or Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs, was the Yuan dynasty office that administered Buddhist clergy and governed Tibet. Founded as the Zongzhi Yuan in 1264 under the Imperial Preceptor Phagpa and renamed in 1288, it worked through the Sakya hierarchs,…

xi-jinping.s: Xi Jinping is a Chinese politician who has been general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party since 2012 and president of the People's Republic of China since 2013. The son of the revolutionary leader Xi Zhongxun, he has concentrated power to a degree not seen since Mao,…

xinmin-hui.s: The Xinmin Hui, or New People's Society, was a mass organisation founded in Beijing in December 1937 under Japanese sponsorship to win support for the Provisional Government of the Republic of China. It promoted a Confucian-based doctrine of cooperation with Japan and…

xoybun.s: Xoybûn ('Independence') was a Kurdish nationalist league founded in 1927 in Lebanon by Kurdish exiles and intellectuals, including members of the Bedirkhan family. It organised and supported the Ararat rebellion against Turkey from 1927 to 1930, led in the field by Ihsan Nuri…

xanthippus-father-of-pericles.s: Xanthippus was an Athenian statesman and general, the father of Pericles. Ostracised in 484 BCE, he was recalled during Xerxes' invasion and commanded the Athenian contingent at the victory of Mycale in 479 BCE.

xiao-ziliang.s: Xiao Ziliang (460–494), Prince of Jingling, was a son of Emperor Wu of Southern Qi and a leading patron of literature and Buddhism. At his estate near the capital Jiankang he gathered scholars and monks, including the Eight Friends of Jingling, and sponsored Buddhist debates…

xincai-county.s: Xincai County is a county in Zhumadian, in southern Henan province, China. Its name means New Cai: the State of Cai moved its capital there from Shangcai in the sixth century BCE under pressure from the State of Chu, before shifting again to Zhoulai in 493 BCE.

xiong-yi.s: Xiong Yi was the traditional founder of the State of Chu, said in the Shiji to be the great-grandson of Yu Xiong. According to that account King Cheng of Zhou enfeoffed him as a viscount at Danyang in the Han River region in the eleventh century BCE, and his descendants of the…

xianyang.s: Xianyang is a city in Shaanxi, on the Wei River west of Xi'an. It was the capital of the State of Qin from 350 BCE and then of the Qin dynasty, where the First Emperor built vast palaces.

xiang-xu.s: Xiang Xu was a minister of the State of Song in the 6th century BCE. In 546 BCE he brokered a peace conference at the Song capital, where fourteen states, led by Jin and Chu, agreed to end their wars and share the leadership of the Zhou world.

ximen-bao.s: Ximen Bao was an official of the State of Wei in the 5th century BCE, governor of Ye under Marquis Wen. He is remembered for ending the local custom of 'marrying' girls to the river god by having the shamans thrown into the river instead, and for digging twelve canals that…

xinzheng.s: Xinzheng is a city in central Henan, south of Zhengzhou. It was the capital of the State of Zheng from the 8th century BCE and, after the State of Han conquered Zheng in 375 BCE, of Han until 230 BCE; parts of the old city walls survive.

xaltocan.s: Xaltocan was an Otomí town on an island in Lake Xaltocan in the northern Valley of Mexico. From the 13th century it ruled a regional state, but around 1395 it was conquered by the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco under Tezozomoc and many of its people dispersed.

xining.s: Xining is the capital of the Chinese province of Qinghai, on the Huangshui river at the north-eastern edge of the Tibetan plateau. In the 11th century, as Qingtang, it was the court of the Tibetan ruler Gusiluo.

xxiv-corps-united-states.s: XXIV Corps was a corps of the United States Army formed in 1944 for the Pacific War. It fought at Leyte in the Philippines and in the Battle of Okinawa in 1945, and under Lieutenant General John R.

xiang-yan.s: Xiang Yan was a general of the State of Chu in the last years of the Warring States period. In 225 BCE he defeated a Qin army under Li Xin, but in 224 BCE Qin sent a much larger force under Wang Jian, which crushed his army.

xiao-cha.s: Xiao Cha (519–562) was a grandson of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty who, after quarrelling with his uncle Xiao Yi, allied with the Western Wei. When Western Wei forces took Jiangling in 554 and killed Xiao Yi, they made Xiao Cha emperor of a small Liang state around the city…

xiao-kui.s: Xiao Kui (542–585) was the second emperor of the Western Liang, a small state around Jiangling that existed as a vassal of the Northern Zhou and then the Sui dynasty. A respected scholar and writer, he reigned from 562 until his death.

xian.s: Xi'an is the capital of Shaanxi province in north-western China, in the Wei River valley of the Guanzhong plain. Nearby lay the Western Zhou capitals Fengjing and Haojing, the Qin capital Xianyang and the great Han and Tang capital Chang'an, on whose site much of the modern…

xipe-totec.s: Xipe Totec, 'Our Lord the Flayed One', was a Mesoamerican god of spring, agricultural renewal and goldsmiths, worshipped by the Aztecs and other peoples. In his festival of Tlacaxipehualiztli, priests wore the flayed skins of sacrificial victims, symbolising new growth…
